comments.body:
Yes, a `fast-review` mode makes sense, but I would make it **delta/context-assisted**, not a blind continuation of the previous agent chat.

Current behavior is intentionally full-review oriented:

- `agent-review.yml` runs two reviewer lanes, Claude and Codex, in parallel, then runs synthesis: [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L119-L229), [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L244-L366).
- Review lanes and synthesis currently use `session_policy: track-only`, so they record run metadata but do **not** restore a previous named ACP session: [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L200-L201), [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L333-L334).
- The docs explicitly call out that repeated review synthesis is one-shot and does not reuse prior conversation state: [`session-continuity.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/session-continuity.md#L14-L20), [`session-continuity.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/session-continuity.md#L86-L90).
- Synthesis already has an important safety rule: do not carry forward old findings unless grounded in current artifacts or current PR state: [`review-synthesize.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L9-L13).

So for question 1: **continuing from the past session is technically possible, but I would not make that the main fast path for review.** It risks stale review memory affecting current-head judgment. Sepo already has session resume/fork machinery in `run-agent-task` and `run.ts`, but review deliberately avoids it today: [`run-agent-task/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L73-L87), [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L445-L559).

Recommended design:

1. Add a `review_mode` input to `agent-review.yml`, defaulting to `full`.
2. Support `review_mode: fast` as:
   - capture current PR head
   - find the latest trusted Sepo review synthesis and its reviewed-head marker
   - if current head is unchanged, reuse/refresh the existing review result instead of rerunning both reviewers
   - if current head changed, run a **delta review** focused on changes since the previous reviewed head, plus unresolved prior action items
   - require synthesis to revalidate every carried-forward finding against current PR state
3. Make fast mode run fewer expensive steps:
   - one reviewer lane instead of Claude+Codex, using configured/default provider
   - optionally skip or defer `rubrics-review`
   - keep synthesis, because it owns final verdict, reviewed-head provenance, inline cleanup, and orchestration handoff
4. Keep `full` as the default for first review, risky PRs, security-sensitive changes, or when no trusted prior reviewed-head exists.
5. Expose it as either `@sepo-agent /review --fast` or `@sepo-agent /fast-review`; internally I’d prefer one route with a mode flag to avoid duplicating dispatch and docs.

Execution plan before coding:

1. Add `review_mode` workflow input to [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml).
2. Thread that mode from [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L905-L922).
3. Add a small typed helper/CLI to locate the latest trusted review synthesis for a PR and compare its reviewed-head marker with the current head.
4. Add a delta-review prompt variant or inject mode-specific instructions into the existing review prompt.
5. Update synthesis prompt constraints so fast mode can consider prior synthesis only as context, never as unverified truth.
6. Add tests for unchanged-head reuse, changed-head delta mode, missing prior synthesis fallback, and stale reviewed-head fallback to full review.
7. Document the mode in action/session docs.

I’d proceed with this only after approval, since it changes review behavior and the default/full-vs-fast tradeoff should be explicit.
Closing because this agent issue has had no activity for 30 days.

title: Consider a "fast-review" mode
